note: Captures produced by a live strongSwan pair. Ground truth is the configuration, not an annotation.

tunnels.name: ikev2-modern
tunnels.note: AES-256-GCM, PRF-SHA2-256, ECP-256, PFS on. The reference posture.

tunnels.name: ikev1-aggressive-dh2048
tunnels.note: Aggressive Mode with 3DES but a 2048-bit group. Paired with T3 this separates the key exchange finding from the cipher finding.

tunnels.name: ikev2-sha256-integrity
tunnels.note: AES-256-GCM with SHA2-256 integrity on a 384-bit curve. A second clean baseline, so a grade of A is shown on more than one configuration.

tunnels.name: ikev2-dh1536
tunnels.note: MODP-1536. RFC 8247 lists this as SHOULD NOT, which is a different severity from the 1024-bit group, and the corpus otherwise only shows the worse case.

tunnels.name: ikev1-main-mode-des
tunnels.note: Single DES under IKEv1 Main Mode. A 56-bit block cipher is a different exposure from 3DES's 64-bit block, and the two are not interchangeable.

tunnels.name: ikev2-null-esp
tunnels.note: A perfect IKE suite protecting data with NULL. The control plane is audited clean and the data plane has no confidentiality at all, which a control-plane-only check would score as healthy.

tunnels.name: ikev2-weak-dh
tunnels.note: MODP-1024 key exchange. RFC 8247 marks this MUST NOT.

tunnels.name: ikev1-aggressive-3des
tunnels.note: IKEv1 Aggressive Mode, PSK, 3DES, no PFS. The headline finding.

tunnels.name: ikev2-x25519
tunnels.note: X25519 with AES-256-GCM. Modern suite, shorter rekey.

tunnels.name: ikev2-legacy-integrity
tunnels.note: SHA-1 integrity. Demoted to MUST- rather than prohibited.

tunnels.name: ikev1-main-mode-3des
tunnels.note: IKEv1 Main Mode with 3DES and MODP-1024. Same ciphers as T3 with the exchange type changed, so the 3DES finding can be separated from the Aggressive Mode finding.

tunnels.name: ikev2-aes192-3des-esp
tunnels.note: A modern IKE suite protecting data with 3DES. IKE and ESP are negotiated separately, so a tunnel can be strong at the control plane and weak at the data plane.
